articleTitle: Transient Responses of a Mode-III Crack in a Piezoelectric Semiconductor Material
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The transient responses of a Mode-III crack in piezoelectric semiconductor materials under combined anti-plane shear mechanical and in-plane electrical impacts are investigated in this article. During the solution, the standard integral transform and singular integral equation techniques are applied, and the dynamic intensity factors and energy release rate are obtained in the time domain. Numerical results indicate that the fracture parameters are critically dependent on the conductivity of the material. The conclusions in this article may be useful for the design of semiconductor devices.

articleTitle: A Low-Frequency Multi-Resonant Wideband Acoustic Tube Transducer
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The longitudinal vibration broadband transducer is often used in acoustic tube transducer because of its high hydrostatic pressure resistance and its special installation mode. In this paper, a low-frequency multi-resonant wideband acoustic tube transducer is designed and fabricated by the combination of an active piezoelectric ceramic stack and two passive compliant materials. The transducer operates in a frequency band of 3kHz-5kHz, with a height of about 262mm and a maximum diameter of about 57mm. The experimental results show that the low frequency acoustic performance of the transducer is good and the bandwidth of the low frequency multi-resonance transducer can be broadened.

articleTitle: SH0 Wave Transducer Based on YbBa3(PO4)3 Crystal for High Temperature Structural Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)

However, it is very challenging to excite and detect pure SH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> wave achieve high temperature SHM due to the limitation of materials. Both numerical simulation and experimental results show that the YbBP-based transducer is capable of exciting and receiving pure SH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> wave in the four main directions (0°, 90°, 180° and 270°) with a wide working frequency (150 kHz ~ 400 kHz), exhibiting its great potential for application in the high temperature SHM.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis Technology of Gearbox of Mine Hoist
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The working environment of mine hoist is complex, and it is easy to break down. In this paper, the constrained independent component and fast Fourier transform (FFT) energy spectrum analysis are combined. First of all, the mathematical basis of FFT and constrained independent component and the basic principle in fault diagnosis are introduced. Then through industrial experiments, it is verified that constrained independent components can extract fault diagnosis features accurately. Finally, the two methods are combined to make a simple diagnosis of the device. By analyzing the vibration intensity, it is concluded that the vibration intensity at the measuring point 11 is large. The vibration signals of measuring point 2, measuring point 6 and measuring point 10 in the vertical, horizontal and axial directions are analyzed and diagnosed accurately. Through analysis, it is concluded that the gear Z1 or gear Z3 on the high-speed shaft of the gearbox may be worn or pitted. In addition, the transmission shaft of gear Z3 may be misaligned due to wear of the coupling or bearing block. The results show that the combination of these two methods can successfully extract the fault features and accurately identify the fault location.

articleTitle: An Electrode Cleaning Strategy Based on Ultrasonic Microrobots
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Commercial portable electrochemical sensors have rapidly developed in recent years, the decreased detection accuracy caused by contamination is still a huge challenge. Here, an electrode decontamination strategy based on microrobots powered by ultrasound was designed to realize the electrode regeneration. Basic configurations about the manipulation-integrated sensor platform (MISP) are proposed to enable the dual functions of electrochemistry detection and electrode regeneration. Two different vibration modes of the MISP are used to excite enrichment and separation, respectively. Subsequently, we designed and characterized the cleaning microrobots and discussed its role in electrode regeneration. At last, the effects of electrode regeneration are verified with H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensors. The active method mentioned in this work based on microrobots and acoustic manipulation paves the way for electrode regeneration during detection, enabling electrochemical sensors to be more favorable for myriad applications in future.

articleTitle: Research on a Planar Hydrophone Integrated With an Acoustic Baffle Based on Local Resonance Principle
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Hydrophones are usually affected by platform structural noise when working underwater. In order to suppress the adverse impact of the low-frequency structural noise, a new acoustic baffle consisting of a locally resonant acoustic metamaterial with broadband, low-frequency and high absorption coefficients was designed. The reflection and absorption coefficients of the acoustic baffle with air backing were analyzed by the finite element method, and samples were fabricated for performance verification. A planar hydrophone integrated with the acoustic baffle was developed to reduce the adverse impact of forward reflected sound waves and backward radiated noise, and the receiving sensitivity and directivity of the baffle hydrophone were analyzed theoretically. This work investigates the potential of metamaterials in hydroacoustic applications and makes contribution to the improvement of the platform-mounted hydrophone design.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis of Ventilator Blades Based on Non-Contact Measurement Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Taking the axial flow ventilator as the research object, the non-contact measurement technology is adopted to carry out fault diagnosis by detecting the gap transformation between the fan blade blade edge gap and the casing. According to the mining ventilator blade structure, operation characteristics and common blade fault types to build fault diagnosis test bench, combined with blade vibration, leaf tip gap transformation and other parameters for multi-information fusion, to obtain the working state of the blade; through the normal blade and fault vibration tests and comparisons, the use of the Hilbert yellow - transformation and other signal analysis means, extracted the non-contact measurement method of the blade under the normal signal and fault signal characteristics, improve the real-time measurement of blade faults. The characteristics of normal blade signal and fault signal under non-contact measurement method are extracted by using signal analysis means such as Hilbert Huang-transform to improve the real-time diagnosis ability of blade fault. The results show that it is feasible and effective to utilize the non-contact measurement method of blade edge gap detection for fault diagnosis of fan blades.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional DtN-FEM Scattering Analysis of SH Guided Waves by Surface Plate-Thinning Defect in a Plate
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient technique called two-dimensional Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) finite element method (FEM) to analyze the scattering of Lamb guided waves through a plate with surface defect. Utilizing the mode orthogonality, the unknown tractions at virtual boundaries are expressed in terms of the unknown scattered displacements at virtual boundaries via scattered coefficients. After that, this relationship at virtual boundaries can be finally assembled into the global DtN-FEM matrix to solve the problem. Compared with the traditional FEM, this method has the advantage of dimension reduction and need no absorbing medium or perfectly matched layer (PML) to suppress the reflected wave. Besides that, the reflection and transmission coefficients of each guided mode can be obtained by simple post-processing using FEM configurations.

articleTitle: Study on Thermal Energy of Three-Dimensional Propeller Anti-Icing Electrothermal System
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: As aircraft icing has received more and more attention, aircraft icing and anti-deicing technology are becoming one of the focuses of researches in the field of aerodynamics. At present, the main ice protection system are thermal anti-icing and piezoelectric vibration anti-icing system. Although researchers have carried out a lot of research, the existing researches mainly focus on the numerical calculation of fixed-wing aircraft icing. There are few researches about the anti-icing effect of three-dimensional propellers. In this paper, the electric anti-icing thermal load characteristics of a typical three-dimensional propeller are investigated, and the influence of different parameters on the anti-icing thermal load of the propeller is analyzed. Relevant results have reference significance for the design and optimization of anti-icing system.

articleTitle: Dynamic Response of Multi-Span Continuous Bridge Above Canyon Subject to SV and P Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The amplifying effect of ground motion in canyons is a major threat to the safety of ground structures. In order to further study the influence of ground motion on ground structures in canyons, a multi-span continuous bridge based on semi-circular canyons is built in this paper. Using viscoelastic artificial boundary method and ground motion input method, the seismic response of canyon terrain under SV wave and P wave of vertical incidence and oblique incidence are analyzed, and the ground motion time history is obtained, which is used as the seismic input at the pier support point. Under simplified soil-structure interaction, the dynamic response of a multi-span continuous bridge under earthquake is analyzed by using multi-point transient input method. The numerical results show that the canyon topography has an important effect on the ground motion, and the dynamic response of the canyon bridge is sensitive to the incident Angle and the incident wave frequency, and the time history difference of the multi-point seismic displacement input plays a major role in the response of the canyon bridge. At present, there are still many neglected factors in the research of canyon bridge ground motion, and further research needs to be supplemented. The results of this paper can provide reference for the seismic design of bridge structures built in complex terrain.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Performance Analysis of Single Crystal Vector Hydrophones With Laminated Beam Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In order to enhance the performance of the underwater vector receiving sensing, we develop a two-dimensional co-oscillating PIMNT single crystal vector hydrophone with a laminated beam structure. The vector channels consist of two orthogonal single crystal laminated-beam accelerometer, featuring a three-layer structure of metal layer-soft interlayer-metal layer. To facilitate a comprehensive analysis, we fabricate a single crystal laminated-beam vector hydrophone sample, as well as a control group consisting of a single crystal metal-beam vector hydrophone, a piezoelectric ceramic laminated-beam vector hydrophone, and a piezoelectric ceramic metal-beam vector hydrophone. The test results reveal that the single crystal laminated-beam vector hydrophone manifests the highest sound pressure sensitivity of surpassing -191~dB and the deepest directional notch of about -30~dB at a frequency of 200~Hz, compared to the control group. In addition, the laminated-beam vector hydrophones have lower resonant frequencies than the metal-beam counterparts. These findings verify the performance superiority of the single crystal laminated-beam vector hydrophone in terms of the sound pressure sensitivity and the directional sensing.

articleTitle: Impact Monitoring and Positioning Method of Steel Plate Based on Piezoelectric Acoustic Sensor Array
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, an impact stress wave analysis method to indirectly represent the impact force is introduced by using a high-sensitivity quartz crystal piezoelectric acoustic sensor array. The finite element simulation method is used to establish an acoustic-solid coupling model. The difference in the flight time of array sensors is calculated to locate the impact position. Besides, a multi-channel acoustic wave signal acquisition and processing system has been developed in the LabVIEW platform, where a MATLAB based signal processing model is combined to perform the Fourier transform and calculate the flight time difference. The simulated annealing algorithm is adopted to optimize the experimental scheme and accurately monitor the impact location. The impact experiment results are compared with the actual impact coordinates, offering the maximum absolute error of less than 3 cm. The impact monitoring and positioning system has a broad application prospect in the field of structural health monitoring.

articleTitle: Ice Adhesive Strength on the Surfaces With Shallow Groove Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Icing is an inevitable problem for most aircraft and has caused many accidents since decades ago. Many de-icing countermeasures have been prompt, such as electric heating, plasma synthetic jet, vibration, and so on. A combination of surface characteristics and piezoelectric vibration de-icing has been paid a lot of attention for its energy-saving capability. However, a more precise power release is always desired, which requires a more accurate estimate of ice adhesive strength. Hence, we conducted our investigations on the ice adhesive strength regarding surfaces with shallow grooves. We validated that a decrease in freezing temperature leads to an increase in ice adhesion. The reason could be a decrease in grain size. The patterns of how shallow grooves affect the ice adhesion correlates well with one of our earlier studies and suit the semi-empirical estimation well if adequate equalization was made.

articleTitle: Damage Identification Method Based on PZT Admittances and a Multi-Task Network Model
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A damage identification method based on a multi-task deep learning network and Bayesian fusion is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the 3D finite element model of a cantilever steel beam with three surface-bonded piezoelectric ceramic (PZT) transducers is established and validated experimentally. The admittance signals of PZT under different damage scenarios will be obtained by simulating the damage with a cut on the beam. Next, the admittance data are input into the constructed multi-task network model for training and validation. Then, the test data are input into the trained model, and the damage of a steel beam is located and quantified to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Finally, Bayesian fusion is used to fuse the identified results based on single PZT admittance signals at different positions to improve the accuracy of damage identification.

articleTitle: Wave Propagation Characteristics of Piezoelectric Fg-Cntrc Plates
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The problem of the dynamic response of a structure is fundamentally caused by the propagation of elastic waves in the structure, so the study of wave propagation characteristics is of great importance for analyzing mechanical behavior of the structure. This paper investigated the wave propagation characteristics of infinite piezoelectric carbon nanotube reinforced composite (FG-CNTRC) sandwich plates. Based on the third-order shear deformation theory, the dynamic kinetic equations for sandwich panels were developed by using the Hamiltonian principle. According to the displacement form function of the infinity plate, the dispersion characteristic equation for piezoelectric FG-CNTRC sandwich plates is derived. By the solution, the dispersion relations are obtained. On this basis, the effects of parameter variations on wave propagation characteristics are discussed.

articleTitle: The Vibration Analysis of Layered and Braided Cylinders for the Determination of Material Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In modern products from advanced manufacturing processes, annular cylinders of different materials and configurations are widely utilized for essential functions such as loading resistance, material delivery, shielding, housing, and power transmissions under various service conditions. To ensure the proper design and manufacturing of such cylindrical components, material properties, processing techniques, and parameters must be known for evaluation and quality assurance. In this study, a three-dimensional mathematical modeling of the braided cylinders with different material layers is made in the cylindrical coordinates, and the Rayleigh-Ritz method is employed to establish the eigenvalue equation for vibration frequencies with the consideration of the primary boundary conditions. By combining the Resonant Ultrasound Spectroscopy (RUSpec) technique with the calculated resonant frequencies of the sample in good agreement, the material properties are extracted with the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Propeller Icing Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This study addresses the critical safety issue of ice accretion on propellers in aircraft, helicopters, and aerial vehicles operating in extreme weather conditions. Propeller icing alters aerodynamic characteristics, impacting overall flight performance. Existing de-icing solutions, including piezoelectric de-icing and Vibration de-icing, remain limited due to a lack of systematic research. The paper employs numerical simulations to comprehensively investigate propeller icing characteristics, focusing on droplet impact, ice accretion, and aerodynamic effects. Results highlight primary collection areas, the influence of velocity and rotational speed on collection rates, and aerodynamic impact. The study contributes innovative insights, aiming to enhance understanding and propose effective solutions for safe aircraft operation in adverse weather conditions.
