articleTitle: Piezoelectric-Fiber-Optical Online Sensing of Lightning Strike-Induced Guided Wave Responses in Aircraft Composite Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Guided wave detection can be used as a promising technology of lighting strike monitoring for aircraft composites, during which the online lighting strike-induced guided wave response sensing under the harsh lightning environment remains a challenge. A high-reliability piezoelectric-fiber-optical online sensing method is studied in this paper. In the method, the lightning strike-induced guided wave responses are online sensed by PZT wafers integrated with the composite structures. Furthermore, to avoid the severe effects of lightning current coupling and EMI, the photoelectric conversion transmission is particularly adopted to transmit the guided wave responses to the following data acquisition system. The lightning strike-induced guided wave responses, with high SNR and free of crosstalk, can be thus online acquired. With the basic principle of piezoelectric online sensing firstly analyzed, the piezoelectric- fiber-optical online sensing method is developed and finally validated by a lightning strike experiment on a carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) composite plate.

articleTitle: Research on Plane Stress Measurement Method For CFRP Based on Array LCR Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Stress concentration occurs in composite materials during preparation, processing to assembly and service, and it is crucial to conduct stress detection on them. Composite materials have anisotropic properties, resulting in complex ultrasonic stress relationships. In this paper, an array ultrasonic critical refractive longitudinal plane stress measurement method is proposed. Aiming at the interference of noise on the calculation results of acoustic time difference, a multi-resolution wavelet noise reduction algorithm is designed to process the echo signal. In order to verify the feasibility of the method, stress loading experiments were carried out on Carbon fibre reinforced plastics (CFRP) specimens in the range of 0–160 MPa, and the results showed that the stress measurement error was less than ±8.96 MPa and the angular measurement error was less than ±6.87°. The CFRP structural components in the wing box section specimen were tested for assembly stresses, which provides a basis for future internal stress testing experiments on composite structural components of aircraft.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Active Vibration Control of a Cylindrical Shell
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the dynamic modelling, active vibration controller design and simulation analysis for a cylindrical shell equipped with piezoelectric sensors and actuators. Based on Donnell-Mushtari shell theory, the kinetic equations of piezoelectric plate and cylindrical shell coupling are derived by using Hamilton principle. The first six natural frequencies and modes of the cylindrical shell were analyzed by ANSYS. To verify the validity of the simulation analysis, an aluminum shell was fabricated. In the experimental analysis, the first six natural frequencies of the cylindrical shell are measured by the accelerometer and compared with the simulation analysis. The first two free vibration modes agree well with the simulation results. Finally, the piezoelectric active control of cylindrical shell is simulated by sine wave and MATLAB. The simulation results show that the piezoelectric actuator and the proposed controller can effectively suppress the vibration of the cylindrical shell.

articleTitle: Hashin-Shtrikman Bounds for Piezoelectric Composite Materials with Periodic Distributed Inclusions
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The prediction of effective moduli of piezoelectric composites is one of the most important topics in composite materials. Early studies on the effective moduli of piezoelectric composites were mainly about ellipsoidal inclusions. This paper proposed the variational bounds for piezoelectric composite with cubic inclusions periodically distributed, which is an extension of Mejak's work on the elastic composites with periodic microstructure. This methodology is available for the prediction of the effective modulus bounds of the piezoelectric composites with inclusions of different geometries if the Hill tensors of the inclusions are available. The variational bounds for piezoelectric composites with cubic and spherical inclusions are respectively evaluated. The results show that the effective modulus bounds of the two piezoelectric composites is quite similar with each other. The maximum relative error is about 5%.

articleTitle: Vibration and Sound Insulation Characteristics of Functionally Graded Sandwich Plates of Variable Thickness Type Under Elastic Boundary Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The free vibration and sound insulation characteristics of functional gradient sandwich plates (FGM) with variable thickness are examined under various boundary conditions. The dynamic model of FGM sandwich plates is established from an energy standpoint using the modified Rayleigh-Ritz method and the fluid-solid coupling conditions based on the first-order shear deformation theory. The numerical solution is compared with the analytical solution of the FGM sandwich plate. The results show that the theoretical model of the FGM sandwich plate is accurate and effective. Then the impacts of various factors on the vibration and sound insulation performance of variable thickness FGM sandwich plates are analyzed.

articleTitle: Study on the Propagation Characteristics and Experimental Detection of Guided Waves in Cement Grouted Bolts
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Due to the advantages of high sensitivity, low attenuation and long detection distance, the ultrasonic guided wave method is suitable for the quality detection of anchor bolts. However, the prerequisite for the application of this nondestructive detection method is to have a deep understanding of the propagation characteristics of guided waves in cement grouted bolts. In this paper, the propagation characteristics of longitudinal guided waves in cement grouted bolts are investigated based on the Kelvin-Voight viscoelasticity theory and using the Legendre polynomial series method. The effects of material viscoelasticity on the guided wave speed and attenuation are investigated. Meanwhile, an experimental testing platform for ultrasonic guided waves in cement grouted bolts was built to analyze the effects of different anchorage lengths on the propagation characteristics of guided waves.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Active Vibration Control of Space Truss Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A novel active vibration control method utilizing embedded piezoelectric actuators is proposed for micro-vibration of space truss structure. The embedded piezoelectric actuators are incorporated at the intersection of the truss structure and base. When the truss structure experiences vibration from external excitation or substrate disturbance, acceleration sensors monitor the response at the top of the truss structure. In order to generate an additional vibration with the identical frequency of the external excitation but in the opposite direction, and with equal amplitude, the embedded piezoelectric actuators are applied with a specific electrical signal. Through the synthesis of vibrations, the amplitude of the structure is reduced to achieve active vibration control. Firstly, the effect of various layout schemes of piezoelectric ceramics on the actuator performance is analyzed using the finite element method. Secondly, a prototype of the embedded piezoelectric actuator is manufactured and the truss structure is constructed. Finally, the complete measurement system is constructed and the experiment is conducted to investigate the effect of vibration suppression. The results indicate that the embedded piezoelectric actuators hold an effective vibration reduction in the active control system of the space truss structure. Especially for vibration in the high-frequency range and during resonance, the vibration suppression effect on vibration is more noticeable, reaching a maximum of -25 dB. Meanwhile, the method possesses a straightforward structure, reduced cost, lower installation and maintenance complexity. These factors provide valuable references for implementing piezoelectric active control design within a large-flexible structure in space.

articleTitle: Weak Nuclear Radiation Signal Reconstruction Methods Based on Improved Sparsity Adaptive Greedy Pursuit Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Nuclear material and nuclear technology have widely been used in many fields of our society, which can bring us great benefits, but also darkle great threats to us. Therefore, it is of important significance to study the effective nuclear radiation detection method and strengthen the nuclear radiation detection in the application of nuclear material and nuclear technology. Aiming at the weak nuclear radiation signal detection problem, by analyzing the characteristics of nuclear radiation pulse signals and studying the traditional nuclear radiation detection methods, a new weak nuclear radiation signal reconstruction method based on the improved sparsity adaptive greedy pursuit (SAGP) algorithm and its two fused methods were proposed in the paper. Firstly, an adaptive Gabor redundant dictionary was established on the basis of the characteristics of nuclear pulse signals. Then, an improved SAGP algorithm and its two fused algorithms namely the sparsity adaptive greedy matching pursuit (SAGMP) algorithm and the sparsity adaptive greedy orthogonal matching pursuit (SAGOMP) algorithm were given. Finally, the proposed methods were tested by using the measured nuclear pulse signals. Experiments show that the proposed methods can accurately reconstruct the amplitude and time of weak nuclear pulse signals to achieve the detection on weak nuclear radiation signals well.

articleTitle: Propagation of Coupled Acoustic, Electromagnetic and Spin Waves in Saturated Ferromagnetoelastic Solids
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: We study the propagation of plane waves in an unbounded body of a saturated ferromagnetoelastic solid. Tiersten's equations form small fields superposed on finite initial fields in a saturated ferromagnetoelastic material are employed, with their quasi static magnetic field extended to dynamic electric and magnetic fields governed by Maxwell's equations for electromagnetic waves. Dispersion relations of the plane waves are obtained. The cutoff frequencies and long-wave approximation of the dispersion curves are determined. Results show that acoustic, electromagnetic and magnetic spin waves are coupled in such a material. For YIG which is a cubic crystal without piezoelectric coupling, the acoustic and electromagnetic waves are not directly coupled but they can still interact indirectly through spin waves.

articleTitle: Helical Gear Transmission Fault Diagnosis Based on Improved Empirical Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Compared with spur gear transmission, helical gear transmission in the early fault or single tooth dominant fault, due to its high contact ratio, smooth transmission and other advantages. Fault characteristics are more subtle and difficult to extract caused by the weak vibration impact fault of the helical gear. In this paper, therefore, the helical gear vibration fault signal is collected through the integrated electronics piezoelectric (IEPE) accelerometer. Then, the fault signal spectrum is adaptively divided into multiple intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) based on the improved empirical wavelet transform. Next, the fault characteristics of the interesing IMFs are extracted through envelope demodulation spectrum, so as to achieve the fault feature extraction and diagnosis of the helical gear. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the method are verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Design of a Mode-Coupling Transducer Based on Relaxed Ferroelectric Single Crystal
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The transmitting power of traditional CLASS V flextensional transducer is not high. To solve this technical problem, the application of new active material, structural design and parameter optimization methods are adopted. The relaxed ferroelectric single crystal piezoelectric material polarized along the [011]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> direction is effectively used, and its piezoelectric coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{32}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{31}$</tex> are high. The displacement amplification structure is added, and the material and size of the structure are optimized. Finally, the working frequency of the transducer is reduced and the power is increased. The active material is more fully utilized, and a technical way to improve the power of the transducer is provided.

articleTitle: Design and Simulations of a High-Temperature and High-Pressure Acoustic Logging Piezoelectric Transducer
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In ultra-deep wells above 8000 m where the bottom hole temperature exceeds 230°C, it is difficult for existing logging instruments to satisfy the requirements of high temperature and high pressure resistance. In this paper, a novel design of high-temperature and high-pressure resistant logging acoustic transducer is proposed, in which the laminated piezoelectric transducer is solid-filled instead of conventionally liquid-filled. Through the finite element multi-physical simulations of the logging acoustic transducer, the vibration modes, stress distribution and sound field distribution are analyzed to optimize the transducer structure parameters. When a 200 MPa ultrahigh pressure is applied around the logging acoustic transducer, the results show that the maximum stress on its piezoelectric plate can be reduced to less than 5 MPa after structural optimization. In addition, the sound field distribution and directivity of the logging acoustic transducer are also analyzed and performed well, which provides technical guidance for physical manufacturing.

articleTitle: Guided Waves in One-Dimensional Hexagonal Quasicrystal Cylindrical Structures With Sectorial Cross-Sections
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The double Legendre polynomial method is employed to investigate the guided wave propagation in one-dimensional hexagonal quasi-crystal cylindrical structures with sectorial sections. The influence of the phonon-phason coupling effect, variations in structural parameters (radius-thickness ratio and central angle) and quasi-periodic direction on the wave characteristics are studied. The cut-off frequencies of phonon and phason modes are inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area.

articleTitle: Vector Characterization of the Sound Field in the Sonar Domes
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The research direction of this paper is based on the acoustic environment of underwater unmanned vehicle (UUV) outboard platform, with the help of finite element simulation, using COMSOL to model the outboard platform equipped with vector array, to study the noise vector characteristics inside the deflector shroud under the influence of flow noise at a certain air speed, and to analyze the changes in the shape and size of the deflector shroud, as well as the changes in the vector acoustic characteristics caused by the changes in the placement position of the vector hydrophones, in order to obtain the optimal installation position and selection of the size of the vector hydrophones. To obtain the optimal installation position of the vector hydrophone and the size of the fairing.

articleTitle: The Forced Vibration and Transmission Stability of Printing Moving Web
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The forced vibration characteristics of printing moving web are investigated using the Differential Quadrature Hierarchical Finite Element Method (DQHFEM). Firstly, the mechanical model of printing moving web under the action of external excitation force is established. The variational formula of the web is derived in terms of the Hamilton theory, and the Gauss-Lobato is employed to discretize the vibration variational formula. Secondly, the transverse deflection basis functions are constructed by applying the higher-order quadrature hierarchical unit, and the natural frequency of the web is solved. Finally, through numerical analysis, the law of the influence of velocity on the dimensionless natural frequency of the web is obtained, and the interval in which the moving web is in steady-state operation is determined. The results show that the method has excellent numerical stability and convergence for studying the forced vibration characteristics of printing moving web and preventing the occurrence of resonance phenomena.

Author Keywords: The Differential Quadrature Hierarchical Finite Element Method

articleTitle: High-Frequency Vibration of Beveled Crystal Plates by Using Subregional Geometric Fitting Method
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The high-frequency vibrations of AT-cut beveled quartz resonators are studied in this work based on Mindlin's theory and Subregional Geometric Fitting Method (SGFM). Quartz crystal plates with nonuniform thicknesses are partitioned into three regions and fitted in each region by using the polynomial functions and the measured geometric morphology data. The governing equations obtained are based on Mindlin's two-dimensional theory and the coupled vibrations are further solved using the partial differential equation module of COMSOL. In numerical calculations, we compared the results of SGFM with the those of global fitting method. The accuracy and effectiveness of the SGFM were also verified. It is has found that the frequencies obtained through the SGFM are slightly higher than the frequencies obtained through the global fitting method. Meanwhile, as the beveling time increases, the frequency increases and the energy trapping effect becomes more obvious. The proposed method can significantly improve the computational efficiency of thickness-shear vibration while ensuring accuracy, and is expected to provide a new geometric fitting method for the analysis of beveled quartz crystal resonators.

articleTitle: Development of a Multichannel Piezoelectric Ultrasonic Transducer Array for Nondestructive Testing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Welded structures have been widely used in automotive production, aerospace, construction industry and other fields. With the trend of industrial welded structures becoming larger and thicker, it is of very importance to test the weld quality of the medium-thickness steel plates above 25 mm for ensuring the safety and reliability of the weld structures. In this paper, a multi-channel piezoelectric ultrasonic transducer array has been developed for detecting the sub-millimeter defects inside medium-thickness steel plates. Both the electrical impedance analysis and ultrasonic pulse echo test characterization show that the theoretical design model can effectively guide the design of the ultrasonic transducer array design. Besides, a standard butt-welded steel plate was tested for weld defects with a minimum feature size of 0.5 mm, and the results show that the developed multi-channel piezoelectric ultrasonic transducer array can accurately detect sub-millimeter weld defects, with a detection resolution of better than 0.5mm.

articleTitle: Coupling of Nonlinear Isolated Waves With Hygrothermal Damage Composites
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Based on the interaction between the isolated wave generated in the one-dimensional particle chain and the composite laminate damaged by damp heat, the mechanism of the coupling action between the isolated wave and the stiffness degradation of the composite laminate after the damage is studied by establishing a model of the stiffness degradation of the composite laminate, establishing the differential equation of the coupling action between the isolated wave and the composite laminate, solving the differential equation by the fourth-order Runge-Kutta method and changing the working temperature and humidity, obtaining the relevant characteristics of the reflected isolated wave by numerical calculation, exploring the relationship between the rebound parameter information of the isolated wave and the temperature and humidity, and providing a theoretical basis for the nondestructive testing of the composite laminate structure under the influence of damp heat.

articleTitle: Stress Analysis of Torpedo Homing Transducer Under Impact Load
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In the process of entering the water, the self-guided transducer array built in the head will be subjected to huge impact load. Once the self-guided transducer is damaged, the torpedo will lose the ability to track the target underwater. In this paper, the force analysis of torpedo self-guided transducer under shock state is carried out. Combined with the equivalent circuit model of the self-guided transducer, the sound field transmission model and the impact response of the self-guided transducer are given. In addition, the finite element simulation of the self-conducting transducer is carried out to analyze the transient response of the self-conducting transducer when the head of the transducer is hit by a big impact, and the displacement distribution and stress distribution of each part of the self-conducting transducer are given.

articleTitle: Design of Surface Acoustic Wave Magnetic Field Sensor Based on Multilayer Composite Thin Film Ta/TbDyFe/Cr
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Using multi-layer composite Ta/TbDyFe/Cr film as the sensitive material, a surface acoustic wave(SAW) magnetic field sensor with high sensitivity and long-term stability is optimized. We developed a delay line SAW device with a center frequency of 150 MHz, using radio frequency(RF) reactive magnetron sputtering to deposit Ta/TbDyFe/Cr film on the delay line of the SAW device. Then, we integrated the coated device and the uncoated device into a differential oscillation circuit. Under the action of magnetic field, the magnetostrictive effect produced by TbDyFe film causes the propagation speed of SAW to change, then the corresponding differential oscillation frequency change is used to evaluate changes in magnetic fields. In order to further improve the long-term stability of the sensor, a 30 nm Cr transition layer and a 10 nm Ta protective layer were introduced. The experimental results show that the developed magnetic field sensor has long-term stability and high sensitivity (6.55kHz/mT).

articleTitle: The Effective Properties of One-Dimensional Orthorhombic Piezoelectric Quasicrystal Materials Containing Ellipsoidal Inclusions
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Eshelby tensors serve as the basis of micromechanics which should be explored first to study the effective mechanical behavior of heterogeneous materials. In this paper, the Eshelby tensor is generalized from isotropic materials to quasicrystals. By utilizing Green's functions and Cauchy's residue theorem, simple and unified expressions of Eshelby tensors for one-dimensional (1D) orthorhombic piezoelectric quasicrystal are derived. Specifically, the closed-form Eshelby tensors are given when the shape of the inclusions is elliptic cylinder. Furthermore, the effective stiffnesses of 1D orthorhombic piezoelectric quasicrystal are obtained in view of the received Eshelby tensors and the Mori-Tanaka mean theory. Finally, parameter studies are carried out, and the effect of material properties and volume fraction on the effective overall material properties are investigated.

articleTitle: Actively Regulating Total Internal Reflection in Elastic-Dielectric Elastomers Bi-Materials Using Biasing Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper deals with the reflection and transmission of SH waves at a well-bonded interface separating two dissimilar isotropic elastic and dielectric elastomers (DEs) solids subjected to biasing fields. A solution is proposed to regulate the total internal reflection (TIR) behavior of the interface through pre-stretch and preset electric displacement. The mechanical model and solutions for the dynamic analysis of the elastic-DE bi-materials were established based on the nonlinear electroelastic framework of Dorfmann and Ogden, and related linear small-increment motion theory. The reflection, transmission and energy coefficients at different incident angles and biasing fields are given in the numerical calculation. Numerical results show that the TIR behavior depends strongly on the incident angle, pre-stretch and preset electric displacement of the SH waves, and the necessary condition for the occurrence of TIR under the biasing fields is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt{K}\leq \lambda \overline{D}_{3}^{1/6}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Coupling Field Analysis of a Piezoelectric Simply Supported Plate Based on Double Fourier Series and Truncation With Fixed Products
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this work, the coupling field analysis of piezoelectric simply supported plates is studied by the method of truncating high-order terms with fixed products (TFP). When comparing the truncation of high-order terms with fixed values (TFV), TFP can more accurately find the parts with smaller errors in the double Fourier series expansion, reduce the number of calculated terms, simplify the calculation process, and solve the actual problem. Experimental results show that the computational efficiency of TFP is higher than that of TFV when double Fourier series expansion is adopted. The convergence and precision of TFP are better than those of TFV. When the piezoelectric plate is thick, the shear stress changes along the thickness direction, which cannot be ignored.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to an Inverse Problem of Heat-Source Detection in a Piezoelectric Semiconductor Plate
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A heat source in a piezoelectric semiconductor plate can result in an electric potential well, which blocks the electric current and change its electric behaviors. On the contrary, the measured current fields can be inversely mapped to the position and magnitude of the corresponding heat source, which can be applied to heat-source detection. This heat-source detection problem is difficult to be calculated using traditional computation methods, such as finite element analysis. In this paper, deep learning (DL) methods are investigated to solve the heat-source detection problem. DL models are trained on datasets that contain pairs of induced current fields and heat sources to learn the mapping relationship. The trained DL models can predict the position and magnitude of heat sources given the input current fields. This learning capacity of DL models provides an effective tool for heat-source detection.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Guided Wave Pipeline Defect Detection Based on Spectral Subtraction
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper aims to establish a pipe model using COMSOL to simulate the process of piezoelectric plate excitation of L(0,2) longitudinal mode guided waves and analyze the echo results of its L(0,2) mode. And an experimental platform was built, using 16 length telescopic piezoelectric ceramic pieces for synchronous excitation, and 16 piezoelectric ceramic pieces for reception in the same direction. In this paper, spectral subtraction is used to process the echo signal, which removes the inherent noise frequency in the pipeline, improves the SNR of the echo signal, and optimizes the sensitivity of the defect identification in the pipeline.

articleTitle: A Study on High-Frequency and Symmetric Vibrating Mode of Rhombic Piezoelectric Actuators
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper utilizes a dynamic stiffness model to analyze and calculate the static and dynamic characteristics of the rhombic displacement amplifying mechanism under fixed-vibrating mode and symmetrical vibrating mode. Modal analyses of the rhombic piezoelectric actuator are carried out under fixed-vibrating constraint and symmetric constraint. The simulation results show that the resonant frequencies of the actuator in bending vibrating mode under fixed-vibrating and symmetric constraints are 724.61 Hz and 1806.15 Hz respectively, which is close to the calculated results. Static characteristics are also calculated and analyzed. The resonance frequency of the symmetrical vibrating mode is significantly higher than that of the fixed-vibrating mode, which can verify the validity of the proposed dynamic stiffness model. On account that the output performance is proportional to the vibrating amplitude and frequency of the rhombic actuator, a high-performance symmetrical vibrating device can be expected.

articleTitle: Research on Vibration Isolation Performance of a Metamaterial With Negative Poisson Ratio
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Regulation low-frequency noise and vibrations is always a challenging issue in engineering. Metamaterials represent a novel class of materials distinguished by their special mechanical properties. Through meticulous material and structural engineering, regulation of the sound wave transmission can be achieved. A model with a tetragonal negative Poisson ratio is proposed and its transmission properties is thoroughly analyzed. Investigating the impact of structural parameters on band characteristics reveals the regulation mechanism. In the bandgap, the model demonstrates outstanding vibration isolation performance, achieving isolation effects exceeding −100 dB for displacement excitation. Fine-tuning unit sizes and array parameters lead to adjustment of the vibration isolation frequency band, resulting in excellent performance. Specifically, the vibration isolation performance first increases and then decreases as the cone angle θ decreases. It amplifies as the feature length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b$</tex> increases. The relationship between the modals corresponding to certain energy bands and vibration isolation was also studied. The vibration isolation band is offset to a lower frequency by introducing a mass block. Efficient vibration isolation in the frequency range of 80~2000 Hz can be achieved within a thickness of 30 mm, meeting predefined performance standards.

articleTitle: On the Feasibility of Soft Magnet Array for Switch Application
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Soft magnetic materials have the advantages of good softness and flexibility, and can be used in the fields of soft robotics, actuators, flexible electronics and other fields. They can also be used for soft magnetic switches according to their actuating and sensing mechanism. At present, most switch materials are hard materials, with poor flexibility and impact resistance. In some application scenarios, it is hoped that switches have better flexibility and flexibility in terms of materials and actuation. Based on the rapid development of soft magnetic materials, the emergence of soft magnetic switches further expands the application of soft magnetic materials in the fields of sensing and actuating. This paper proposes an array structure with multiple magnetization directions, and reports a soft magnet switch array for planar surface applications.

articleTitle: Online Stress Characterization of CFRP Plates Based on Multi-Frequency Lamb Wave Group Delay Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This paper presents a stress monitoring scheme for carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) plates based on the acoustoelastic effect of Lamb waves. The scheme fully integrates redundant information and improves the accuracy of stress characterization. While Lamb waves offer abundant information due to their dispersion characteristics, they also pose challenges for feature extraction. Additionally, the high sampling rate of traditional strategies limits the real-time performance of monitoring systems. To address these issues, a group delay extraction method based on Gaussian pulse fitting is applied. In regions where wavenumber and frequency are approximately linear, the dispersion distortion response under Gaussian excitation is a new Gaussian function, which is the basis of high-precision delay parameter identification. Finally, laboratory experiments are conducted to evaluate the performance. After calibrating the stress coefficients, a tensile test is carried out within the range of (0–150) MPa. The maximum error is 13.2 MPa. The experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve high-accuracy stress characterization.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis on Anti-Plane Shear Response and Wave Superposition in Grillage Above Hollow
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A multipoint transient input method (MTIM) is proposed based on analytical displacement field. The method mainly considers the time difference of wave propagation, and highlights the time difference of multipoint inputs. The feasibility of the method is verified by three analytical cases on wave responses of semicircular hollow-grillage model. The analytical solution on the displacement field of half space with semicircular hollow under the incidence of anti-plane shear waves (SH waves) is solved by the elastic wave theory, and the correctness and stability of the solution are verified. Based on the modified time-frequency transformation method (MTFT) and MTIM, the transient displacement responses of grillage plate are derived. The influence of incident angle, form of grillage, wave velocity ratio and other factors is discussed. The numerical results show that the surface hollow and above factors will have a significant impact on the response of grillages. This paper aims to give an effective analytical method for the wave propagation characteristics in structures and provide theoretical reference for wave protection and detection engineering of structures.

articleTitle: Doping Effects of MnO2 Additives on the PZN-PZT Ternary Piezoceramics
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: High-Qm piezoelectric ceramics have widespread applications in acoustic, ultrasonic sensors, resonators, and piezoelectric actuators due to their efficient energy conversion and transmission capabilities. This study investigated the doping effects of MnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> additives on the structures and electrical properties of the 0.3Pb(Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</inf>Nb2/3)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-0.7Pb(Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.52</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.48</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ternary piezoceramics. The research findings demonstrate that MnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> addition enhances the sintering process, resulting in improved density and grain size, reduced dielectric loss, and increased mechanical quality factor. Notably, doping with 0.5 wt. % MnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> achieves the highest mechanical quality factor and minimal dielectric loss. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing the performance of piezoelectric ceramics.

articleTitle: Fractional Order Control of Vibration in Flexible Electronic Moving Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Flexible printed electronic films are susceptible to vibration caused by external interference due to their minor stiffness, thus affecting the quality of printed matter, so active vibration control is necessary. An integer order controlled vibration method containing a model of fractional order terms is employed for active control over flexible printed electronic films. Firstly, a fractional order damping term on top of the integer order dynamics equation is introduced and the spatial equation of state is obtained by equating the fractional order transfer function with that of the integer order by using the Oustaloup filter. Secondly, the optimal controller for active control is designed using the LQR control method, and the vibration control of flexible printed electronic films is realized. Finally, the control emulation indicates that the LQR control can decrease the amplitude without changing the resonance frequency of the flexible printed electronic films. The effects of fractional order control on the vibration control of flexible electronic films are shown to be able to achieve the desired control effect.

articleTitle: Analyisis of Response Time of Flexiblepiezoelectric Sensors With Stress Wave Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Flexible piezoelectric sensors with fast response time are required in the field of human motion detection, personal health monitoring, and artificial electronic skin. By employing stress wave theory, the model for response time is established. The model indicate that the response time of flexible piezoelectric sensors decreases with an increase in the relaxation time of the piezoelectric material. The reduction in response time can also be achieved by increasing the elastic modulus and density of the piezoelectric material or by decreasing the thickness of the piezoelectric layer. The response time model introduced in this paper could potentially provide a means to manufacture flexible piezoelectric sensors with exceptional ultrafast response capabilities.

articleTitle: Coupling Effects of Interfacial Diffusion and Sliding on Electro-Mechanical Behaviors of Laminated Plates With Embedded Piezoelectric Layers
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The time-dependent responses of an angle-ply laminated plate with an embedded piezoelectric layer in cylindrical bending is investigated based on the state-space method. Both the interfacial diffusion and sliding are considered to simulate the interlaminar imperfect bonding. Besides, a matrix reduction technique is adopted to establish the global transfer relations of the elastic variables between the piezoelectric layer and the elastic strip. Then, the exact solutions are obtained by solving a set of differential equations with respect to time. The numerical investigation indicates that the coupling effects of the interfacial diffusion and sliding should be considered carefully for the analysis of an imperfectly laminated structures.

articleTitle: The Effect of Ultrafine Ferroelectric Material Grain Size on Energy Storage Density
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Using molecular dynamics simulation, we conducted a study to investigate the relationship between the hysteresis loop, residual polarization, coercive field, and dielectric constant of barium titanate polycrystals under the influence of different electric fields, in relation to grain size. The smaller the grain size, the greater the electric field required for complete polarization domain reversal. As grain size increases, the non-linear correlation of the ferroelectric hysteresis loop strengthens, but it becomes challenging to achieve saturation polarization at low electric fields. Additionally, we observed the formation, migration, and annihilation of polarization vortex domains. These vortex domains initially appear near grain boundaries, then migrate into the interior of the grains, and eventually vanish. The speed of vortex domain movement is directly proportional to the energy density of the polycrystal. It's worth noting that energy efficiency decreases with the increase of grain size and electric field magnitude.

articleTitle: The Application of ACA and SVD Algorithms in the Matrix Low-Rank Approximation
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Since the adaptive cross approximation (ACA) and the singular value decomposition (SVD) are unsuited for directly decomposing the large-scale matrices, this paper investigates the accelerated algorithm and the accelerated hybrid algorithm for low-rank decomposition of matrices with the scale and elastic wave problems, respectively. The results show that the accelerated algorithm can significantly reduce the low-rank decomposition time for the coefficient matrix of scale wave, and the accelerated hybrid algorithm can effectively compress the tensor form matrix of elastic wave.

articleTitle: A Piezoelectric Energy Harvester Used for Underwater Propeller Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Inspired by the pressure rotation of turbine runner in water flow, a piezoelectric energy harvester used for underwater propeller detection is proposed in this paper. The flexible piezoelectric cantilever beam structure is placed inside the device. The propeller is driven by water flow to stimulate the cantilever beam to generate vibration. The piezoelectric plate on the cantilever beam collects vibration energy and stores it in the capacitor. According to the electromechanical coupling characteristics of the propeller piezoelectric energy harvester, a dynamic model of the system is established. The structure of energy collector is analyzed by finite element method. Modal analysis is used to determine the natural frequency of the structure and the influence of cantilever beam with different thickness on energy harvesting. The output power of piezoelectric plate and the optimum impedance of the device are measured experimentally at different speed of propeller. The optimum impedance is 100k Ω when the propeller speed is 120r/min. When the propeller speed is 300r/min, the output power of a single piezoelectric plate can reach 218µW.

articleTitle: Dynamic Stress Analysis of A Non-Circular Cavity in 2D-Inhomogeneous Medium Under SH-Wave Incidence
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Scattering of SH wave by a non-circular cavity in two-dimensionally inhomogeneous medium is investigated in this work. The non-circular cavity is supposed as a square cavity. Applying complex function method, governing equation of SH wave propagation is solved analytically. Displacements and stresses in the inhomogeneous medium are deduced subsequently. Utilizing conformal mapping method, the interface of the square cavity is mapped to be a unit circle. Dynamic stress concentration factors (DSCF) at the cavity with different inhomogeneous parameters are calculated and analyzed. Numerical results illustrated the DSCF at the cavity is affected by the inhomogeneous parameters evidently.

articleTitle: Method for Measuring Axial Stress in Fluid-Filled Pipelines Based on T(0, 1) Mode Guided Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: This text describes an approach for measuring axial stress in fluid-filled pipelines using T(0, 1) mode guided waves. The method involves using finite element analysis to obtain the dispersion curve for water-filled pipelines. Because the T(0, 1) mode guided wave possesses non-dispersive characteristics and experiences minimal energy attenuation in water, it is chosen for stress monitoring. To successfully excite the T(0, 1) mode guided wave, the paper introduces a design for a ring-shaped piezoelectric array transducer. Simulation results indicate that using this transducer design effectively excites the T(0, 1) mode guided wave. Finally, the paper outlines the design of experiments and the validation of the simulation results.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Scale Ultrasonic Motor Applied to Micro Swimming Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, a micro ultrasonic motor using two orthogonal bending modes is designed, fabricated, and characterized. This motor is mainly composed of two dual rotors and one stator bonded by rectangle piezoelectric ceramics to excite the stator's orthogonal bending modes. The operating principle of the motor design is to utilize the coupling of the orthogonal bending modes to drive rotor. The stator has a diameter of 2.6mm and a weight of 0.338 gram. The vibration characteristics and output performance of the motor are tested. The no-load speed of t the prototype of the motor can be reached 7000 rpm under the driving voltage 180 Vp-p at the driving frequency of 103.6 kHz. The proposed millimeter-scale ultrasonic motor provides a new driving method for micro pipeline swimming robot.

articleTitle: SH Waves in a Bi-Layered Structure Composed by Viscoelastic Material and Piezoelectric Semiconductor
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The dispersion and attenuation characteristics of SH wave propagation in a bi-layered structure composed by viscoelastic material and piezoelectric semiconductor structures are investigated in this study. The analytical solutions of the viscoelastic layer and piezoelectric semiconductor layer are obtained by direct solution method, and the solution of complex domain is solved by minimum modulus approximation method. After the analysis, a biasing electric field is applied along the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_{2}$</tex> direction to slow down the attenuation of the SH wave within the bi-layered structure. When the value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kh$</tex> is small, the SH wave within the bi-layered structure exhibits an amplification phenomenon. While maintaining the constant electric field, increasing the steady state carrier concentration has a more remarkable effect on SH wave amplification. These conclusions can provide a theoretical basis for expanding the application of ultrasonic nondestructive testing in viscoelastic materials.

articleTitle: A Modified Maxwell Model for the Aging of AT-Cut Quartz Crystal Resonators
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Quartz crystal resonators have been widely used in electronic communication products due to their advantages of frequency stability and strong anti-interference ability. However, in the long-term usage, the frequency of the quartz crystal resonator shifts with time, which is known as the aging phenomenon. In the cases when high stability of frequency is required, the frequency shift has a large impact on the applications. Therefore, it is important to establish a feasible model to predict the aging of quartz crystal resonators. In this paper, the potential of the viscoelastic theory in the description of the aging of quartz crystal resonator is discussed. Since the thickness vibration theory suggested the relation between the frequency of quartz crystal resonator and the elastic constants, the frequency of quartz crystal resonator is time-dependent if the elastic constant is replaced by an effective elastic constant, which is time-dependent. The definition of the effective elastic constants is proposed via stress relaxation of the Maxwell mode in viscoelasticity. Furthermore, the time-temperature superposition principle is adopted to predict the aging of quartz crystal resonator at different temperatures. The elastic parameters of the Maxwell mode are the elastic constants of quartz, and the viscous parameters of the Maxwell mode are determined by fitting the proposed theory with the experiment data. Similarly, the movement factors are determined. The results proves that the frequency aging of quartz resonators can be well described by the newly proposed theory.

articleTitle: Research on Preload Characteristics of the Inertial Piezoelectric Actuator
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The inertial piezoelectric actuator is one of the hotspots in precision devices due to its simple structure and control system. However, the output performance of the inertial piezoelectric actuator is greatly affected by the preload. To investigate the influence of the varied preload on the output performance, an inertia piezoelectric actuator is proposed and experimentally investigated. The structure and principle of the proposed motor are first introduced in detail. Then, the flexible structure of the proposed motor is simulated and optimized. Finally, the prototype of the proposed inertial piezoelectric actuator is manufactured, assembled, and experimented. The experimental results show that the preload has a greater effect on the back-ward phase of the stick-slip motion, and the output performance of the motor prototype can be significantly improved by changing the appropriate preload. These results are expected to improve the understanding of the inertial motor performance, providing a reference for the design of future inertial piezoelectric actuators.

articleTitle: Axisymmetric Vibration of Piezoelectric Semiconductor Disc Based on Double Legendre Polynomial Method
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Piezoelectric semiconductors (PSCs) have attracted much attention in recent years for combining piezoelectric with semiconducting properties. As far as we know, there is very limited theoretical research on the vibration problem of three-dimensional PSC disc structure. In this paper, a double Legendre polynomial method was developed to analyze axisymmetric free vibration for axially polarized PSC disc. The present method directly incorporated the boundary conditions into the control equations of PSC. Simultaneously, the mechanical displacements, the electrical potential and the carrier density were defined as the form of double Legendre polynomials series. Then, the natural frequencies are obtained through solving eigenvalue. The numerical example shows that the steady-state carrier density has important influence on the natural frequency only in a certain range, and the effect on the higher modes is more obvious than the lower modes. Finally, the effects of radius-to-thickness ratio on the frequencies were also studied.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of 1-3 Piezoelectric Composite Material Air Coupled Ultrasonic Transducer
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Air-coupled ultrasonic transducers play a crucial role in air-coupled in-situ defect detection techniques. This article focuses on the design, fabrication, and optimization of a high-sensitivity piezoelectric air-coupled ultrasonic transducer operating at a frequency of approximately 220 kHz. To ensure efficient acoustic impedance, a double matching layer structure was devised based on the fabricated piezoelectric material. Matching layer 1 was created using hollow glass microspheres filled with epoxy resin composite material. Interestingly, the addition of a diluent was found to enhance the vacuum degassing effect of matching layer 1. The sensitivity and working efficiency of the air-coupled ultrasonic transducer were further enhanced through the optimization of the matching layer thickness and the matching circuit. By independently optimizing the thickness of the double matching layers, the transducer's sensitivity and bandwidth were increased to -43 dB and 22.7%, respectively. Notably, the performance parameters of this transducer are comparable to, and in some aspects superior to, similar international products.

articleTitle: Design of Radial Composite Longitudinal Vibration Piezoelectric Transducer Excited by Four Piezoelectric Stacks
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: A radial composite longitudinal vibration piezoelectric transducer excited by four piezoelectric stacks is made, which consists of a central coupling metal block, four piezoelectric stacks, four front fan-shaped metal mass and a cylindrical shell. Based on the four-terminal network method and the electro-mechanical analogy principle, the equivalent circuit model of the transducer is established and the resonance frequency equation is derived. The resonance frequency and acoustic performance of the radial composite piezoelectric transducer are analyzed by finite element software. The frequency response, directivity and electroacoustic conversion efficiency of the physical transducer is tested by impedance analyzer and anechoic pool. The theorical, simulative and experimental results show that the radial composite longitudinal vibration piezoelectric transducer excited by four piezoelectric stacks has horizontal omnidirection and high electroacoustic conversion efficiency. The resonance frequency is obtained by equivalent circuit method and finite element, which are consistent with the experimental test results.

articleTitle: Design of a Two-Dimensional Underwater Particle Velocity Pickup Device
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Addressing the subject of a suspended co-oscillating vector hydrophone application platform, a new sound wave receiving theory model of underwater particle velocity pickup sensor was established. Based on the study of the inner sound field of an elastic cylinder vibrating freely under the action of sound waves in theory, the influence of material and geometry parameters on the frequency response of particle velocity has been analyzed. According to the results of parameter optimization and taking into account engineering needs, one sample of two-dimensional particle velocity pickup sensor has been designed and tested. By comparing the results of sensitivity and directivity tested in a calibration device, the general rules of theoretical analysis have been verified. The theory and experiments confirmed the feasibility of particle velocity pickup sensors in engineering applications.

articleTitle: Frequency Shift-Based Debonding Localization of Steel Concrete Composite Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In steel concrete composite structures, the presence of interface debonding damages critically threaten structural integrity, posing significant concerns to safety, serviceablity and durability. Monitoring and detecting such internal interfacial damages throughout a structure's service lifespan is of significant practical importance. While non-destructive testing (NDT) methods are essential for this purpose, conventional NDT techniques, including radiography and magnetic particle testing, possess inherent limitations. This paper introduces a novel interfacial debonding detection technique based on the centroid frequency shift theory. Experimental validation conducted by authors substantiates its precision in identifying debonding regions. Additionally, the proposed piezoelectric sensor module demonstrates strong engineering applicability. This innovation holds significant promise in ensuring the integrity and safety of steel-concrete composite structures.

articleTitle: Design and Characteristics of a Two-Axis Piezoelectric Accelerometer With Right Angle Cantilever Beam
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: An increasing number of individuals are delving into the research of high-precision multi-axis vibration sensors. Traditional multi-axis piezoelectric accelerometers are constructed by orthogonally combining multiple single-axis piezoelectric accelerometers, ensuring no signal coupling among them. However, these kind accelerometers typically exhibit large volume and mass, failing to meet the requirements for miniaturization. In this paper, a two-axis piezoelectric accelerometer is proposed based on the stress-averaged right-angled beam structure. The paper commences with a finite element analysis of the stress distribution within the right-angled beam structure. This analysis confirms that the right-angled cantilever beam effectively smooth stresses on the piezoelectric element, leading to a substantial improvement in the element's service life. Secondly, the paper realizes a double-auxiliary-beam two-axis piezoelectric accelerometer structure. Through finite element simulation, the structure is observed to exhibit favorable frequency response characteristics and low inter-axis coupling, thereby confirming its structural feasibility. The findings in this paper offer valuable ideas for the multidimensional measurement of subsequent sensors.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of Foam-Filled Honeycomb Sandwich Structures Subjected to Underwater Explosion Shock Wave
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Underwater explosions can cause serious damage to structures, which is mainly caused by shock wave action. Composite sandwich structure is a special structure of composite materials. Honeycomb sandwich structure has the advantages of sound absorption, light weight, optimal specific stiffness and specific strength, so it is widely used in aerospace, ships and public facilities. The foam material can effectively absorb the impact energy, but the texture is too soft and the strength is not enough. It can be combined into a new composite material as the filler of the honeycomb sandwich structure, so that it has the buffering performance of the foam and the strength of the honeycomb structure. Based on LS-DYNA, finite element models of different honeycomb sandwich structures with or without foam filling are established in this paper, and the propagation characteristics of underwater explosion shock wave, structural deformation and energy absorption characteristics are analyzed, which provides a reference for the design of Marine sandwich structures and ship protective structures. The results show that the energy absorption characteristics of the similar square honeycomb sandwich structure is slightly better than that of the hexagonal honeycomb sandwich structure, and the foam filled honeycomb sandwich structure has better anti-knock performance, which proves that the foam filled honeycomb sandwich structure has good energy absorption characteristics.

articleTitle: Design of Piezoelectric Temperature Sensor With Resistance to Pressure Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Based on the study of the relevant characteristics of piezoelectric ceramics, the piezoelectric transducers are characterized by fast response and high sensitivity. Meanwhile, the relevant parameters of piezoelectric ceramics are sensitive to the temperature changes. Hence, a piezoelectric temperature sensor is designed in this paper. The paper firstly analyzes the trend of the resonant frequency of the piezoelectric element varying with the external ambient temperature and the pressure changes applied through multi-physical field coupling simulation. The simulation results determine the influence of the temperature and pressure on the resonant frequency of the sensor. Secondly, the relationships between the temperature, the pressure and resonant frequency are verified through a series of experiments. Experimental results show that the piezoelectric sensor designed in this paper is sensitive to the temperature, and the pressure has no effect on the resonant frequency of the sensor in a certain pressure interval. Therefore, the paper realizes a piezoelectric temperature sensor that can withstand the action of certain pressure.

articleTitle: The Experimental Study of Active Surface System for the Large-Aperture, High-Accuracy Radio Telescope
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The correction of deterioration of wavefront errors of the large-aperture, high-accuracy radio telescope due to the deformation of reflective surfaces is an important issue. The actuator sub-module of active surface system directly determines the stability and accuracy of the correction. Here presented is an actuator sub-module for the active surface system, and an experimental study and performance analysis are carried out. The results show that the actuator sub-module can effectively improve accuracy and stability of the correction.

articleTitle: Preparation and Electrical Properties of K/Ce/Sm Co-Doped CaBi2Nb2O9 Ultrahlgh-Tc Piezoelectric Ceramics
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)

The influence mechanism of different doping concentrations of Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>+ and Sm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ on the phase composition, microstructure, and electrical behavior of CaBi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> ceramics is investigated. articleTitle: In-Situ Defect Measurement Method for CFRP Plate Based on Air-Coupled Ultrasonic Lamb Wave
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: The air-coupled ultrasonic technique is capable of in-situ defect measurement for in-service CFRP plates. Traditional air-coupled ultrasonic methods often adopt the XY orthogonal step scanning method. In order to improve the accuracy of defect detection, an in-situ measurement based on the instantaneous energy spectrum of the air-coupled ultrasonic Lamb wave and surround-step scanning method is proposed. 24 air-coupled ultrasonic transducer positions are evenly arranged on a 90mm×90mm CFRP plate to realize 128 defect measurement scanning paths according to the surround-step scanning method. The Morlet wavelet extracts the instantaneous energy spectrum of the Lamb wave of 128 defect measurement scanning paths to obtain the corresponding defect indexes. The ellipse probability damage imaging algorithm and the -6dB method are used to realize the qualitative analysis and quantitative characterization of the delamination defect with a diameter of 10 mm. The absolute error and the relative measurement error of the defect measurement are 4.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 5.2%, respectively. The proposed method is promising to detect small-size defects of CFRP plates in the aircraft skin in situ.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Digital Control Platform for Ultrasonic Peen Forming
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel digital control platform for ultrasonic peen forming (UPF) is proposed in this study to achieve self-adaption during machining for obtaining the desired arc height. First, the structure and self-adaption principle of the platform are explained. Then, the diameter of the pits on the Almen strip after UPF is determined by a laser spectroscopy confocal microscopy to determine that the platform had sufficient accuracy. Finally, Almen strips are processed on this platform and changes in the arc height of the Almen strips under different processing conditions were compared and analyzed to determine optimal machining parameters. From the experimental results, the novel digital control platform for UPF can effectively control the processing parameters, and its flexible machining method contributes to better machining effects. Machining should have the lowest possible offset distance and the highest possible movement speed, and a suitable preload force should be selected.

articleTitle: Study on Injury of the Cytoskeleton and Cytomembrane in Endothelial Cells Induced by Ultrasound
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Low-frequency ultrasound can be applied intravascularly for thrombosis or drug delivery in clinical and experimental studies. However, it is still unclear the biological effects of ultrasound on blood vessels, especially endothelial cells (ECs). The laws of endothelial cytoskeleton changes under ultrasound induction are investigated in this study. ECs are treated with low-frequency ultrasound, and cytoskeletal morphology is analyzed by staining F-Actin. We further analyze the changes of cytoskeleton and cell membrane. Finally, the biological effects induced by ultrasound at the tissue level are studied in an ex vivo blood-vessel model. Significant changes in cell membrane and cytoskeletal structure are detected after ultrasound induction, including cytoskeletal rupture and blebbing. A time threshold of ECs injury is established under different ultrasound intensities. This study illustrates a pattern of significant changes in the structure of ECs induced by ultrasound, which provides a reference for the selection of a safe threshold for ultrasound.

articleTitle: Rapid and Label-Free Detection of Human Epididymal Protein 4 by Piezoelectric Immunosensor
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: In recent years, human epididymal protein 4 (HE4), which is a new tumor marker, has been discovered with high specificity in the diagnosis of ovarian cancer. Current laboratory methods for detecting HE4, such as enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA), have the disadvantages of being time-consuming and requiring labeling steps. In this study, piezoelectric immunosensors were used to measure the concentration of HE4 antigen in PBS solution which containing various concentrations of the antigen. The performance of this immunoassay such as detection range, test time and accuracy were investigated, respectively. The results revealed that the concentration range of HE4 detected was 200–8000 pmol/ml, the analysis time was no more than 30 min and the relative error was less than 5%. Therefore, the proposed rapid and label-free piezoelectric sensing method in HE4 detection has the great potential in tumor markers detection from clinical serum for early ovarian cancer.

articleTitle: Revisiting the Flexoelectricity in a Functionally Graded Dielectric Nanobeam
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Flexoelectricity is a linear coupling between strain gradient (or non-uniform strain) and electric polarization. A bending dielectric nanobeam can induce giant flexoelectricity that can be used for energy harvesting; however, piezoelectricity is suppressed due to sign symmetry of strains. To break the symmetry of strains and incorporate both flexoelectricity and piezoelectricity, a functionally graded material (FGM) beam is studied. This paper reformulates the functionally graded dielectric nanobeam by incorporating the general strain gradient elasticity theory and the Euler-Bernoulli beam theorem. It shows that the non-uniformity not only evoke piezoelectricity but also enhances energy harvesting, comparing with the isotropic material beam. The optimal size of the FGM beam appears around one order of magnitude higher than that of the single material beam, which makes the beam size more justifiable on practical application. This work may be helpful in the analysis and design of smart piezoelectric nanostructures and could shed light on the flexoelectricity energy harvesting.

articleTitle: Influence of Thomson Effect on Nonlinear Thermo-Electric-Mechanical Coupling Behavior of Hybrid Thermoelectric-Piezoelectric Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2023 17th Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications (SPAWDA)
abstract: Hybrid energy harvester with thermoelectric (TE) and piezoelectric (PE) generators can convert heat and mechanical energy into electricity simultaneously. Thermo-electric-mechanical coupling model is quite necessary to predict its performance. Under large temperature difference, Thomson heat cannot be neglected in TE device analyses. In addition, to harvesting higher energy, the PE beam is usually designed for large deformation. This study investigates the effect of Thomson effect and nonlinear vibration on the coupled thermoelectric-mechanical behavior of hybrid TE-PE system. Based on the simplification of heat sink and the thermoelectric model with Thomson heat, the thermoelectric field of TE part is obtained. The heat sink beam of TE part is also the substrate layer of PE part, the governing equation of nonlinear vibration is obtained based on Hamilton's principle. The output power of hybrid system with and without Thomson heat is analyzed. Numerical results show that material parameters and structure dimensions of hybrid energy harvester can influence performance of TE part and PE part simultaneously. When the temperature difference is small, the influence of Thomson effect on the performance of hybrid TE- PE system is weak. Output power of PE part can either be depressed or promoted by the Thomson effect of TE part, depending on the temperature-dependent Seebeck coefficient. As length of PE layer increasing, the heat dissipation effect of heat sink is reduced. This leads to that the temperature difference between the cold-end and hot-end of TE part is decreased, and performance of TE part is reduced. The paper analyzes the interaction among TE part and PE part in hybrid energy harvester. This study could be useful for guiding the searching for hybrid TE- PE energy harvester which is potentially high performance.
